channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Power On: Exclusive News About Apple’s October Launch Event
item.description: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman exclusively tells listeners about Apple’s plan to pay for influencer travel to their late October launch event. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla Showcases Long-Awaited Roadster With Aerial Tricks
item.description: Tesla finally rolled out its long-delayed Roadster sports car — or rather, launched the vehicle into the sky. The automaker late Thursday held a product reveal unlike any other, showcasing a prototype designed in collaboration with SpaceX outfitted with air thrusters that jumped over other cars and flipped in midair. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Difficult to Overstate' Volatility of White House AI Messaging, Says Greg Allen
item.description: Greg Allen, Founder and CEO of Decision Tree Research and former AI strategy official at the Department of Defense, said that it is 'extremely difficult to overstate' how volatile the Trump administration's messaging has been on artificial intelligence regulations as it swings between dismissing AI safety fears and requiring mandatory regulations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SoftBank Is Said to Weigh Buying Top US Security Firm Allied
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the US, people familiar with the matter said, as founder Masayoshi Son explores ways to deploy AI-powered robots across industries.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo, Min Jeong Lee, Manuel Baigorri and Paula Sambo

item.title: Chip Rout Intensifies and Tesla Showcases Flying Roadster
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down what's behind the chip rout, as chipmakers are set for their longest losing streak since 2008. Plus, shipping estimates for Apple's iPhone Duo slip into January within minutes of the company opening preorders, and Tesla reveals its long-delayed Roadster sports car, showcasing a prototype with air thrusters that flipped mid-air. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Gold Rush Hits America’s College Campuses
item.description: Dorm Room Fund says fears that AI will make college obsolete miss a startup boom already unfolding on campuses. The student-focused venture fund is seeing growing optimism among young founders as AI lowers barriers to building companies and gives first-time entrepreneurs new opportunities. Molly Fowler, founding partner at Dorm Room Fund, joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave, Nscale Put Neocloud Economics in Focus
item.description: Concerns about the enormous amounts of debt financing the AI infrastructure boom are putting the neocloud sector under increasing scrutiny. Decoding Discontinuity CEO Raphaelle D’Ornano discusses the pressure on CoreWeave as interest expenses weigh on its economics. She explains why investors are looking beyond contracted backlogs to financed and energized capacity, and how Nscale’s vertically integrated approach differs as it prepares for a potential IPO. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Longest Chip Selloff Since 2006 Mints Short Sellers $32 Billion
item.description: A historic rout in semiconductor stocks has delivered a windfall for short sellers who were brave enough to bet against what had been one of the highest flying corners of the US equity market for much of the last year.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Reinicke

item.title: US Imposes Drone Flight Restrictions Along Border With Mexico
item.description: The US Transportation Department announced Friday that it’s immediately barring unauthorized drones from flying along the US border with Mexico to help with ongoing security missions, including against illicit cartel activity.
item.dc:creator: Allyson Versprille

item.title: Behind the Scenes of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
item.description: We got an in-depth look at the making of what could be the biggest video game of all time
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: Big Tech Earnings and AI Anxiety
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Fed Chair Kevin Warsh stays silent on rates, fueling bets the Fed holds steady this month. Big Tech earnings kick into high gear as AI anxiety rattles investors. Plus, Tesla’s Roadster takes flight using SpaceX technology. Bloomberg’s Craig Trudell has the reveal, and Ed Ludlow breaks down Netflix’s major shakeup at the top. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: iPhone Duo in Short Supply After Shipments Slip Into 2027
item.description: Shipping estimates for Apple Inc.’s first folding phone slipped into January within minutes of the company taking preorders on Friday, suggesting that strong demand and short supply will make the $1,999 device challenging to purchase on its Oct. 23 release date or in the near future. Bloomberg's Anurag Rana joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla Unveils Roadster With a Nod to SpaceX Merger
item.description: Tesla unveiled its long-delayed Roadster sports car Thursday in Texas, showcasing a prototype that used SpaceX-developed air thrusters to perform aerial flips and accelerate from zero to 60 mph in under one second. Production isn’t expected until 2028, while the flying version will be limited to an invite-only package not approved for public roads. Bloomberg Detroit Bureau Chief David Welch breaks it down on Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We are Only 'Third Inning Relative to this AI Game,' Says Dan Ives
item.description: Three CoreWeave Inc. co-founders have sold $3.3 billion in company shares since last year’s initial public offering, taking money off the table as rising credit risks and investor wariness around AI spending spark volatility in the stock. Dan Ives, Partner at Yorkville & Ives, discusses volatility relative to the AI trade and the outlook for stocks like Coreweave and Apple in particular. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Schwab CEO on AI Strategy, Investing Trends, and ‘Charley’
item.description: Rick Wurster, president and CEO at The Charles Schwab Corporation, discusses customer trends in investing, efforts to attract younger investors, and why the firm is blocking unauthorized AI agents. He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Corrects spelling of “Charley” in video headline) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple iPhone Duo in Short Supply After Shipments Slip Into 2027
item.description: Shipping estimates for Apple Inc.’s first folding phone slipped into January within minutes of the company taking preorders on Friday, suggesting that strong demand and short supply will make the $1,999 device challenging to purchase on its Oct. 23 release date or in the near future.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: CoreWeave Stock Wipeout Exposes Divide Between AI Fear and Greed
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. has become caught in a tug of war between investors who see rising bond yields as a potential rally killer for the AI trade and those who think demand for computing power will make those concerns seem passe before long.
item.dc:creator: Jeran Wittenstein and Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: European Stocks Outperform S&P 500 Amid Rotation Away From AI
item.description: European stocks were set for their biggest weekly outperformance over the S&P 500 since April 2025 as the region benefits from a switch among investors out of the AI trade and from some positive earnings.
item.dc:creator: Macarena Muñoz

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks, Currencies Rebound as Greenback Plunges
item.description: Gauges of emerging-market currencies and stocks gained on Friday as the greenback extended losses and a selloff in shares related to artificial intelligence abated.
item.dc:creator: Peter Laca, Marcus Wong and Maria Elena Vizcaino

item.title: Nscale’s $35 Billion IPO Plans Muddied by AI Data Center Delays
item.description: One flagship AI data center in Norway is six months behind schedule, with workers set to be housed in a floating hotel to get it over the finish line.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon and Paula Doenecke
